title: Coward
text: “I have seen everyone except the wolf man, indeed.”
“Is that so?”

“Indeed. When I tried to escape the loop by pinning my role onto Ren and Itsuki, these were slaves Father had purchased. Both of them showed such loyalty, acting as Father’s right-hand men, that they seemed like thoroughly reliable arms.”
“Huh… is that right?”

What a strange twist of fate, I say. I suppose it just goes to show there’s a real possibility of meeting someone through a broker like this. Given the nature of the place, these were all slaves one could simply buy if one wished to.
“Looking at it the other way, it means they can grow into people worthy of trust, doesn’t it?”
“Indeed.”
I do look forward to seeing how these slaves develop, I say.

“Well, I suppose part of it is that since they’re slotted for the show, they’re not really expected to undergo much training. That goes for the Rabbit-species and the Lizardman. Though the Lizardman’s probably also doing double duty as cargo hauler. And the wolf man is purely for the show—just there to be whipped, I guess…”
Father did mention that using a whip is surprisingly difficult, I say. I imagine he’ll be relying on the slave crest to keep things in line instead.
“Vwooooo…”
The moment the wolf man turned and Father so much as looked at him, the man let out a growl. Father, careful not to let the monster merchant see, let out a small sigh.
“Good enough. I could probably put on a circus with these three right away. Well… though as far as making big money off the show angle goes, that seems like a stretch.”
“I am most eager to see how Shield Hero-sama’s business acumen turns a profit from this. Yes indeed.”
“Before that, I’ve got to train them first, though… kukuku.”
After that, Father registered the slave crests for each of them.
“Haah… haah…”
Then, as if to start with the obvious choice, he approached the Rabbit-species slave first.
“For now, state your names one at a time. You first.”

You understand words, don’t you? Father asked in a voice thick with menace. What was that name again, I wonder? Even back in that loop, Father spoke just as bluntly then too, but… it was so long ago I’ve forgotten most of it. Still, thinking it over again—hypothetically, if Father had chosen this Rabbit-species slave first, then raised Filo-tan next, and I had met them under those circumstances, would I have called this slave Filo-tan’s older brother? Come to think of it, that makes him a sort of “possible older brother,” doesn’t it. Though back then, Filo-tan was already about as tall as Big Sister…
“Guh… T-Theodore.”
Ah, so that was the name. Quite a grand-sounding one, I must say.
“Hmm. Theodore, is it.”

If I were to think of a nickname, Theo or something along those lines would fit, wouldn’t it? Now that I think of it, in this world, people rarely go by nicknames—it’s almost always full names. Even Father called Big Sister by her full name. The exception, I suppose, is when the person themselves goes by a nickname. Fiancée, for instance, sometimes goes by the alias-slash-nickname Mel. As for what Big Sister might be called as a nickname… “Raftha” doesn’t quite roll off the tongue. “Tallia” or something similar would probably be safer. Oh? Now I recall, in the very first world, Father discussed this very topic with Big Sister years later. She’d made a slightly troubled face at the time. Apparently her parents used to call her that, and it stirred up some painful memories. I believe that’s why Father settled on calling her Raphtalia in full.
“Next, you?”
Father turned to the mixed-breed Lizardman and asked.
“C-call me… Shion.”
The slave crest crackled in response. It seemed he had no intention of revealing his real name.
“Hmm… well, fine.”

Once Father gave his consent, the crest settled down. Nice ring to it, Father muttered quietly. Is that so? Well, back when I was in Japan, that was a name I heard quite often—for pigs, that is. There were plenty of Shions. Most of the time, it came from the flower shion, the aster—also known as the “fifteen-night flower.” Its flower language includes things like remembrance and I will never forget you, rather romantic phrases, really. Still, since this one’s clearly going by a nickname or alias, I suppose it’s unrelated.
“And lastly…”
“Vwooo… kuun…”
Father turned his gaze toward the growling wolf man, who, rather than speaking, simply barked like a dog in response.
“Doesn’t understand words?”

“The trouble is, his temperament is quite fierce, sir. Yes indeed. It seems he’s so thoroughly dominated by instinct that proper communication is impossible. However, I can share with you his registered name from the arena.”
The monster merchant offered by way of supplement.
“Good enough. What’s the name?”
“He’s registered as Coward, sir. Yes indeed.”

…Coward, was it? The word means someone timid, spineless, lacking in courage. Well, at least by the standards of English from the world I was born in—my original world, that is. Could an injured slave who once fought in the arena really be named Coward? Father, too, seemed to sense the meaning behind the word, judging by his rather troubled expression.
“How well did this slave perform before he was injured?”

“Well now… by all accounts, quite impressively, sir. Yes indeed. But in what should have been his most important match, he suffered a brutal defeat and injury, which led his employer to demand a hefty sum in damages. He was sold off as a result, and after passing through various hands, ended up here. Yes indeed.”
“What does the name mean?”
“Is there some meaning to it? Yes? I’m afraid I wouldn’t know, sir. It’s likely just some name used in a rural dialect somewhere. Yes indeed.”
So it seems the word carries no meaning in this world’s language. Though I imagine if I put real intent into pronouncing it, even the monster merchant might catch its meaning.
“Coward, I say!”
“Gavuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu!”
The moment I pointed and said it with strong emphasis, the wolf man flew into a rage and let out a furious roar.
“My my, calling him a coward—even Spear Hero-sama provokes him. Yes indeed.”
Father wore an expression of dawning realization, as if it all made sense now.
“Gau! Gauuuuu!”
Baring his fangs fully and snarling at me in threat, the wolf man was met by Father, who stepped in front of me protectively and glared him down.
“Uuuu… kuun…”
“You. What’s your name?”

He’d gone remarkably quiet all of a sudden. Ah, I suppose that must be it—apparently the Shield Hero inspires some strange, indescribable sensation in demi-humans and beastmen. Elephant, too, seemed to nod along naturally the moment she saw Father and heard the words “Shield Hero.” Father has occasionally mentioned something about a weapon’s innate correction affecting things like this. The wolf man clutched his head and shook it side to side.
“My my… as expected of him. Yes indeed.”
The monster merchant looked thoroughly impressed as well—likely concluding that the wild beastman had calmed down thanks to the power of Shield Hero.
“You don’t remember it, is that it?”
He gave a small nod.
“Then… what would you like to be called? As it stands, it’ll be Coward. Both I and this one here will end up pronouncing it as ‘coward’ regardless.”
The wolf man shook his head vigorously, clearly indicating he did not want to be called by that name.
“Then how about an alias—let’s call you Wolf, shall we?”
“Bau!”
That’s the German word for wolf, isn’t it. A bit on the nose, perhaps, but maybe that directness works in its favor. The wolf man, too, seemed to accept the name readily enough.
“Theodore, Shion, and Wolf, then.”
These were Father’s very first slaves in this loop. The wolf man’s level was notably high, but the other two were more or less on par with each other.
“Whatever the case, I accept them. Let’s use these three to make some money, shall we?”
Fufufu… Father laughed wickedly. The monster merchant, apparently swept up in the mood, chuckled along as well. I suppose I ought to laugh along too.
“Kuun.”

Meanwhile, the three slaves stared at us with rather peculiar expressions. And so, that’s how we ended up with three slaves in tow. Incidentally, since the wolf man was noted to have such a fierce temperament, he was fitted with a collar and chain, which Father took hold of himself to prevent any funny business. Apparently the prohibitions bound into his slave crest were also set extremely strict. Given he was such a rampaging wolf, I suppose there was plenty to be cautious about.
